title: Do you think there would be any value in something like this. Screen sharing your gameplay with the ai so you can explain things about the game as you play
author: barret232hxc
selftext:
I use the gemini app alot and you can share your screen and talk to it and have it explain how to do things and it can like highlight stuff. it's really cool. is there anything like that for ai game dev where you could be playing and be like see when I click this button I need it to do xyz and the ai would be like ahah I know exactly what you mean, it would make it more collaborative, but I dunno if that kind of technology exists for the frameworks/workflows we have. I'm kinda new to all this ai stuff but I feel that would be so much smoother than sending screenshots all the time. I'm guessing it would be super expensive but I feel like that's the next level, you're just sitting there creating together and talking about the game even as you're playing it. with the ai and it's seeing everything and talking with you about it while you play

apologies if this is totally something everyone is doing. I find myself constantly out of the loop b/c things move so fast

comments.author: ThreadboundDev
comments.body:
Along a similar vein, I often record videos and share them with Codex for the same purpose.

Most of the time I’ll type out my thoughts or I’ll just share a video and let it tell me its thoughts first and then I’ll explain my thoughts afterwards and I found it’s pretty good at watching the video and understanding it.

It’s been a nice tool in my workflow I feel like

comments.author: EnvironmentFirst4839
comments.body: I build in Godot with Claude + Codex through an MCP. They have direct access to play the game themselves, they do so and take relevant screenshots as proof. I still manually play test everything before merge. If I need to point to a specific component, I just use snip tool… but more likely to just call it by its name and explain what I need done. You should be able to put a name to everything in your product.

replies.author: completelypositive
replies.body:
You can extend this to game mods. 

I modded a wii game and insert AI to control it like an idle game.

comments.author: DerrickBarra
comments.body: I haven't seen that yet, you need a snapshot of the screen, the hierarchy/dom of the application, and the application data state for the agent to make the best use of that idea. The agent wouldn't be tracking you in real time, it would be using snapshots under current tech limitations.

comments.author: VoidHelm_gg
comments.body: Honestly, I think this is way more useful than screenshot-based prompting. The interesting question is whether the AI needs to understand the *game* or just the developer's intent. If it can watch you play and understand “this feels wrong” without you explaining why, that changes the whole workflow.

comments.author: kanyenke_
comments.body: I don't think video works but screenshots often do
